newsitem.title: USA: House puts off farm spending bill until next week.
newsitem.headline: House puts off farm spending bill until next week.

text.p: The U.S. House has delayed work on a fiscal 1998 agriculture department spending bill until next week following a protest by House Democratic women.
During floor debate Thursday, the Democratic women used a series of procedural votes to block work on the bill.
The women said they were protesting decisions made by House Republican leaders regarding which amendments could be offered to a Foreign Appropriations spending bill next week.

The women were upset in particular with an amendment approved for floor debate that would reinstate a "gag rule" on international family planning and eliminate the United States' contribution to U.N. population programs.
An alternative bipartisan amendment was not allowed to be offered, they said.
In face of the women's protest, the House voted 344-73 to suspend work on the bill. The House will not return for legislative business until Tuesday.
